doc.title: Derek Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Majesty of the Seas, May 29, 1995

chapter: The Tonight Show and famous accompaniments
title: Accompanying Pavarotti on Good Morning America
summary: Called at the last minute, Smith waited for Pavarotti and ended up playing We Wish You a Merry Christmas.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: Some of the most fun people you backed up.

Well, lots of people. It wasn’t on that particular show, I’m trying to think of that particular show, but really the funniest story was it wasn’t the Tonight Show, but it was at the same time. I came home from work and I think it was after Benny and there was a message from our service, we all belonged to this service it was called. And my wife had said that the Registry called, you’ve got to be at ABC Television at 5:30 it’s the Good Morning America show, you know, it’s a network show, you’ve got to accompany Pavarotti. And that was the end of the message. So it was already one o’clock, you know.

Yes, so I said it’s too late now to start getting the opera books out and start practicing, so I just got up early and go into town, at least there’s no traffic going to town I’m already there. So I’m there for the 5:30 rehearsal, the show goes on at 7 AM, you know. And so I’m getting a little antsy. I said well at least we should run down this stuff, you know. So I’m looking at my watch, 6:00 comes and no Pavarotti, 6:15, and I’m starting to get a little nervous. And so at quarter to 7, I was supposed to go on at 7, the door opens, and in comes this great big guy, you know, this presence. And he makes, goes to the lady producer and starts putting his arms around her and is making out with the lady producer, and I’m running around saying, “where’s the music?” And I finally get his attention, it’s 5 to 7 now. Funny. And I said, “I’m the pianist, which aria are you going to sing? You know, give me a shot, we’ve got to rehearse it.” “Oh,” he says, “see my manager.” I says, “where’s the manager?” So he says, “that little guy in the corner.” So I find the little guy © Fillius Jazz Archive -9-

in the corner, he’s got this briefcase. I said, “I’m the pianist for Mr. Pavarotti. Which aria is he going to sing?” So the guy opens the thing, and he gets me out this old piece of music, I look at and it says “We Wish You A Merry Christmas.”
